2028 BMW i3 Touring Spied With Roof-Mounted Emergency Lights
17 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
The electric brother of the 3 Series Touring has picked up an interesting accessory. The latest prototype of the i3 Touring carries emergency vehicle lighting on its roof, something the carparazzi haven't encountered on previous test vehicles of the NA1. Obviously enough, those lights are there because the automaker is developing a new member of the BMW Authority Vehicles family.
Before going any further, BMW Authority Vehicles come in many shapes and sizes. From the 1 Series all the way to the 7 Series and X7, these purpose-built machines are modified by the German manufacturer for government agencies, customs, medical, fire, and police duties. A white-painted prototype with blue roof lighting, meanwhile, suggests emergency services and police homologation.
The combination of a longroof with fleet-vehicle white paint and blue lights, on the other hand, suggests operational roles. Think rapid-response vehicle or highway patrol vehicle. It's also worth mentioning that BMW has a thing for equipping pre-production or early-build vehicles like this for internal emergency response at its production facilities, including Munich and Dingolfing.
Beyond the roof-mounted light bar, this prototype does not show any other modification. Camouflaged like there's no tomorrow out back and up front, the i3 Touring wears aero-conscious black machined wheels that frame silver brake calipers. As such, the prototype clearly isn't based on the M Performance model that is expected to be called M60 xDrive.
The rest of the lineup should comprise the 50 xDrive, 40 xDrive, and the rear-wheel-drive 30, with production scheduled to start in July 2027. Based on this information, the i3 Touring is a 2028 model by US automotive standards. Whether the i3 Touring is coming to the United States, we do not know for certain.
Photo: SH Proshots Back in June 2026, the North American vice prez of product management acknowledged that the M5 Touring outsells the sedan, making a case for more exciting wagons in the United States of America. While there may be momentum in the market, with customers also petitioning for the M3 Touring, an electric wagon is very different from one powered by a singing inline-six engine.
The wheels in question, which form a five-pointed star with their spokes, are standard in Germany on the 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive versions of the sedan. Unfortunately, the camouflage makes it impossible to determine the visual package that BMW specified for this prototype. Nevertheless, the longroof in question has the same proportions teased by its maker back in March 2026.
Two months later, back in May 2026, former chief executive officer Oliver Zipse shared even more teaser images of the i3 Touring. He also stated the 3 Series Touring is very popular with business customers and families, hence BMW's decision to add the i3 Touring to the 3er's range. Just like the sedan, the roomier specification will be assembled at BMW Group Plant Munich in Germany.
Because of the wheels, it's natural to assume that BMW is testing either the 40 xDrive or the punchier 50 xDrive here. The lesser dual-motor powertrain is listed with 275 kW (369 hp) and 520 Nm (384 lb-ft) on tap, along with a driving range of up to 710 kilometers (441 miles) on a full charge of its 82.8-kWh battery.
Stepping up to the 50 xDrive means 345 kW (463 hp) and 645 Nm (476 lb-ft) in optimal conditions, along with no more than 912 kilometers (567 miles) from 108.7 kilowatt-hours. Being a wagon, the i3 Touring 50 xDrive should be heavier than its four-door brother, whose 0-60 estimate in the US is 4.5 seconds. Even if it would need 4.6 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph), that's plenty quick for a family hauler, police, or rapid-response vehicle.
